about: LA Century Law is a personal injury firm with offices in Los Angeles, Tarzana and San Bernardino.

The firm states that it works on a contingency fee, with nothing to pay unless the case is won; the first consultation is free; its intake line is open around the clock. It publishes material in English and Spanish.

completeness.note: Categories, opening hours and photo count come from the Places API. The owner's own description, the services list, the Q&A and recent posts are owner-side fields the API does not expose at any price, so they are not scored either way. The API does expose Google's editorial summary, which is a different thing: Google writes those about notable places and has written one for no firm in this directory.

G1.source: the State Bar of California's licensee search
G1.evidence: 7 of 7 named attorneys hold an active California licence and none carries an adverse status

G2.source: the State Bar of California's licensee search
G2.evidence: No named attorney carries a disbarment, a suspension or a disciplinary resignation on the State Bar of California's record, across the 7 we identified. Administrative suspensions, which the State Bar states are non-disciplinary, are not counted here

G3.evidence: 3 physical locations verified on Google Business Profile. California publishes no business register we are able to query, so the registration itself is not verified here. The state's own business search is the place to check it.

G5.evidence: Site has served over HTTPS, a working phone number published, 7 named attorneys published.
G5.source: Public crawl of the firm's own site

G6.evidence: 819 public client reviews across 3 Google listings, above the 10 minimum, and the firm's domain has been registered since 2019-01-24, so it has been operating for more than a year
G6.source: Google Places API and the domain's registration date over RDAP

fee_statement: Many personal injury lawyers work on a contingency fee basis, which means they only get paid if you win your case.

accountability.evidence: no bar or trial lawyers' association named on the pages we read · no professional liability cover disclosed, which is not scored here: plaintiff firms in this market do not publish it, and an absence shared by every firm separates none of them

score.verdict: 4 of 5 eligibility gates passed. 1 could not be answered from the available records (G3) and does not count against the firm. Strongest pillar: C; most headroom in pillar A (2/25).
